newsitem.title: GERMANY: Pressure mounts on Bonn to place Eurofigher order.
newsitem.headline: Pressure mounts on Bonn to place Eurofigher order.

text.p: Pressure mounted on Tuesday for the German government to make a firm order for the Eurofighter combat jet as the German contractor in the four-country project and aerospace workers said thousands of jobs were at stake.

Chancellor Helmut Kohl's government is trying to squeeze military spending as part of general austerity plans, but faces accusations of holding up the project after Britain announced last month it would buy over 200 Eurofighters.
Manfred Bischoff, chief executive of Daimler-Benz AG aerospace unit Dasa, said on Tuesday that an order must be made this year.
"Anything else would have lasting negative consequences for the programme," Bischoff said.
Highly-qualified jobs, plants and know-how could be lost, Bischoff said in a statement after meeting politicians from Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD).
Dasa is working with British Aerospace, Italy's Alenia SpA and Spain's CASA on the Eurofighter.
Workers' leaders from the aerospace sector also warned that up to 18,000 jobs could be lost -- 7,000 of them at Dasa -- if no immediate decision were taken to order the Eurofighter.
Peter Meinck, speaking on Tuesday in Munich, accused Defence Minister Volker Ruehe of not backing the project and failing to come up with an offer.
A source at the defence ministry said talks on financing and pricing Eurofighter were continuing, but could not say when there would be a result.
He said spending cuts meant that defence procurement was having to be cut. "We are working in completely different circumstances," the source said.
Kohl's government plans to reduce military spending by 500 million marks ($330 million) next year to 46.6 billion marks.
-- Douglas Busvine, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($ = 1.521 German Marks)
